description:
This role is for one of our clients 
 Compensation: $70 - $90 per hour 
 
 Employment Type: Independent Contractor
 Work Arrangement: Fully Remote
 Working Schedule: Flexible – Work on your own schedule
 Payment Frequency: Weekly via Stripe or Wise
 About the Role
 We are seeking experienced Kubernetes Engineers with strong production-level expertise in container orchestration, cluster operations, and cloud-native infrastructure to contribute to an AI research initiative focused on improving advanced AI models.
 In this role, you will evaluate the quality, correctness, and production-readiness of Kubernetes tasks used to train and assess frontier AI systems. You will review cluster-operation scenarios, Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, deployment configurations, and troubleshooting workflows to ensure they reflect real-world infrastructure engineering practices.
 Your hands-on Kubernetes experience will be essential in identifying configuration errors, networking issues, storage failures, security vulnerabilities, resource-management problems, and gaps in operational reliability.
 You will provide structured, rubric-based feedback to help establish reliable evaluation standards and improve AI model performance on complex Kubernetes and infrastructure engineering tasks.
 Requirements 
 Key Responsibilities
 1. Kubernetes Cluster Operations & Evaluation 
 Evaluate Kubernetes tasks and cluster-operation scenarios for technical accuracy and production-readiness.
 Review Kubernetes environments deployed on Amazon EKS, Google GKE, Azure AKS, and self-managed clusters.
 Assess cluster architecture, workload orchestration, deployment configurations, and operational workflows.
 Identify issues affecting cluster availability, scalability, performance, and reliability.
 Evaluate whether proposed solutions follow Kubernetes best practices and production-level engineering standards.
 2. Kubernetes Manifests & Helm Chart Review 
 Review and validate Kubernetes manifests, including Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and Ingress resources.
 Assess Helm charts, templates, values files, and deployment configurations for correctness and maintainability.
 Identify configuration errors, resource misconfigurations, dependency issues, and deployment failures.
 Evaluate resource requests, limits, probes, scheduling policies, and workload configurations.
 Ensure infrastructure definitions accurately reflect intended application behaviour.
 3. Cluster Internals & Troubleshooting 
 Assess Kubernetes networking components, including CNI, DNS, service discovery, and ingress configurations.
 Review persistent storage configurations involving PersistentVolumes (PV), PersistentVolumeClaims (PVC), and storage classes.
 Evaluate RBAC policies, service accounts, permissions, and cluster security configurations.
 Analyse common Kubernetes failure scenarios, including CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, scheduling failures, pod eviction, and node-level issues.
 Review troubleshooting approaches and determine whether proposed resolutions address the underlying root causes.
 Assess cluster recovery procedures, fault tolerance, and operational resilience.
 4. Production Readiness & Reliability 
 Evaluate workload stability, resource utilisation, autoscaling, and cluster capacity management.
 Assess high availability, failure recovery, and deployment strategies.
 Review observability, monitoring, logging, and alerting configurations.
 Identify potential operational risks and recommend improvements to cluster reliability and performance.
 5. Research Collaboration & Technical Feedback 
 Collaborate with AI researchers, infrastructure engineers, and platform specialists to improve Kubernetes evaluation tasks.
 Provide clear, structured, and actionable written feedback based on predefined evaluation rubrics.
 Translate practical Kubernetes engineering expertise into measurable standards for assessing AI-generated infrastructure solutions.
 Help refine benchmark tasks and evaluation methodologies to improve technical accuracy and consistency.
 Required Qualifications & Skills
 Professional Experience 
 Minimum 3+ years of hands-on production Kubernetes experience .
 Experience managing, deploying, and troubleshooting Kubernetes clusters in production environments.
 Practical exposure to managed Kubernetes services such as Amazon EKS, Google GKE, or Azure AKS, or self-managed Kubernetes infrastructure.
 Strong understanding of container orchestration, cluster administration, and cloud-native application deployment.
 Kubernetes Architecture & Cluster Internals 
 Deep understanding of Kubernetes architecture and core components.
 Strong knowledge of container networking, including CNI, DNS, service discovery, and ingress.
 Experience with persistent storage, including PV, PVC, and storage management.
 Strong understanding of Kubernetes RBAC, service accounts, and access-control mechanisms.
 Ability to troubleshoot common failure scenarios such as CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, scheduling failures, and pod evictions.
 Configuration & Deployment Management 
 Hands-on experience authoring, reviewing, and debugging Kubernetes manifests.
 Strong familiarity with Helm charts, templates, and package management.
 Ability to evaluate deployment configurations, resource allocation, health probes, and workload scheduling.
 Experience debugging live cluster incidents and resolving production infrastructure issues.
 Programming Skills 
 Proficiency in at least one programming language:
 Go
 Python
 TypeScript
 Ability to read, understand, and troubleshoot scripts and automation used in Kubernetes environments.
 Analytical & Communication Skills 
 Strong troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and problem-solving capabilities.
 Ability to assess complex infrastructure scenarios and identify subtle configuration or operational issues.
 Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to provide precise, structured, and actionable technical feedback.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) or Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD).
 Experience with service mesh technologies such as Istio.
 Knowledge of autoscaling mechanisms, including Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA).
 Experience with monitoring and observability tools such as Prometheus and Grafana.
 Previous experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), platform engineering, or infrastructure operations.
 Prior experience in code reviews, technical assessments, or task grading.
 Familiarity with cloud-native architecture and production infrastructure best practices.
 Contract & Payment Terms
 Engagement will be on an independent contractor basis.
 The role is fully remote and offers flexible working hours, allowing you to complete assignments on your own schedule.
 Project duration may be extended, shortened, or concluded early depending on business requirements and individual performance.
 Payments will be processed weekly through Stripe or Wise, based on services rendered.
 The role will not require access to confidential or proprietary information belonging to any current or former employer, client, or institution.
 Candidates requiring H-1B or STEM OPT sponsorship are not eligible for this opportunity at present.
